findings.title: Delete routing spec contradicts the prescribed cleanup path for stale shared-file copies
findings.description: The Data Flow section specifies "**Delete:** mirrors write — deletes from whichever project file the key's scope maps to", and states `migrate-personal` is "the one exception that touches the *other* project file". For a personal key this means `cf config unset git.integration_branch --project` only touches `.context-forge.local.toml`. But the Collision semantics section (line 146) directs the user to clear a stale shared-file copy via "a separate, explicit `cf config unset <key> --project`", and Verification Walkthrough step 9 (line 259) asserts that this exact command clears the stale copy from `.context-forge.toml` and leaves `cf check` clean. Under the stated delete routing, step 9 is unreachable: `unset` would delete the *personal* copy (the developer's preferred value) while the stale shared copy survives the read fallback — inverting the intended outcome and leaving the `personal-config-in-shared-file` finding permanently unfixable by any documented command except hand-editing. The requirement left unmet is the design's own promised explicit cleanup path for the collision case. Fix: specify that project-scope delete for a personal key also removes any pre-existing copy in the shared file (read-side fallback mirrored on the delete side), or otherwise reconcile the two sections.

findings.title: "Reusing the pattern already used for personal ignores" has no referent
findings.description: Technical Scope says the `cf init` change works by "reusing the pattern already used for personal ignores", but the design's own `.gitignore handling in cf init` section (line 159) confirms "no gitignore-writing logic exists anywhere in `packages/cli`/`packages/core` today" — so there is no existing pattern to reuse. The normative section is self-contained and correct (create-if-absent, append-if-missing line check), so this is a wording issue only, but the phrase could send an implementer looking for scaffolding that does not exist.
